origin.note: Verbatim source of every rule in this file. The original file is left untouched and remains the authoritative source text.
lines: Every input of green color is accepted
Every input of blue color is accepted
Every input of orange color is accepted
Every input of majesta color is accepted
Every input of indigo is accepted
Every input of purple is accepted
Every input of violet is accepted
Every input of Red should be questioned with # Why did you choose Red#
Every input of yellow should be questioned with # Why did you choose Yellow #

decisions.question: "majesta" is not a standard colour name. How should it be interpreted?
decisions.consequence: The rule is kept with the source text unmodified and colour_name "magenta". It is not silently renamed in the origin lines above.

decisions.question: What should the system do when an input matches an "accepted" rule?
decisions.answer: Answer affirmatively and store the preference, only after explicit consent.
decisions.consequence: No preference record is written without consent = true. The answer is produced whether or not consent is given.

decisions.question: Which inputs do the colour rules apply to?
decisions.answer: Only a colour chosen from the palette.
decisions.consequence: Text that mentions a colour name, images and audio are out of scope in this version and must be reported as unsupported, not silently interpreted.

decisions.question: Which numeric value represents each named colour?
decisions.answer: The CSS named-colour value of the same name (CSS Color Module Level 4).
decisions.consequence: Values are verifiable against a public standard instead of being chosen arbitrarily. Example: 'green' is #008000, not #00FF00 (which is 'lime').
